meta.sourcing_rule: every field value is drawn only from the sources listed, consulted in this session, and cites them per field in the record's sources map; a field no consulted source supports is null and carries a verify entry naming it. TA names are not asserted anywhere in this tranche (no TA2 list consulted). The tranche is two organ records plus two sourced-text records for the parts of the system the dataset does not carry at all — the drainage pathway and the lymphoid tissue; no geometry is invented for them and their absence from the dataset is recorded on each.

records.name: Spleen
verify: relations: no value asserted — the consulted TeachMeAnatomy page's relations table did not render in the fetched text, and no other consulted source states the spleen's relations; the field stays null rather than unsourced
ta_name: not asserted — no TA2 term list was consulted in this session
records.note: The release's only intraperitoneal lymphoid organ and, with the thymus, one of only two lymphatic organs it carries at all.
records.position: The spleen lies in the upper left quadrant of the abdomen, under the diaphragm and the ribcage; it is not normally palpable (S1). It is intraperitoneal except at its hilum (S1), and is about 12 cm long, attached to the lateral border of the stomach by the gastrosplenic ligament (S2, S1).
records.internal_structure: An oval organ with a weak capsule (S1), a diaphragmatic surface against the diaphragm and a visceral surface carrying the hilum, with notches on its anterior and superior borders (S1). Internally, the red pulp filters the blood that passes through it, and the white pulp — lymphoid tissue arranged around a central arteriole — mounts the adaptive immune responses (S2). The release carries no concept for the pulp, the hilum or any other part of the spleen (probe-verified), so this structure is sourced text on the whole-organ record.
records.function: The spleen filters the blood, removing old red blood cells, and carries cell-mediated and humoral immune roles (S1); its red pulp is the filtration tissue and its white pulp the adaptive-response tissue (S2). It is fragile — it has no strong capsule (S2) — and its arterial tree divides into vascular segments, which is what makes subtotal splenectomy possible (S1).
records.arterial_supply: The splenic artery — the cardiovascular module's record artery.splenic-artery — arises from the coeliac trunk, runs along the superior border of the pancreas within the splenorenal ligament, and divides into five terminal branches with no anastomoses between them, defining the spleen's vascular segments (S1).
records.venous_drainage: The splenic vein — the cardiovascular module's record vein.splenic-vein — leaves the hilum and joins the superior mesenteric vein to form the hepatic portal vein (S1).
records.lymphatic_drainage: Lymph follows the splenic vessels to the pancreaticosplenic lymph nodes and onward to the coeliac nodes (S1). Neither node group exists as a concept in the release (probe-verified), so this drainage is sourced text only.
records.innervation: Sympathetic supply reaches the spleen from the coeliac plexus (S1).

records.name: Thymus
verify: arterial_supply: no value asserted — none of the sources consulted in this session states the thymus's arterial supply; the field stays null rather than unsourced
ta_name: not asserted — no TA2 term list was consulted in this session
records.note: The release carries the thymus as an organ only in the PART-OF table, filed under the contents of the anterior mediastinum; the IS-A table carries only its lobe line.
records.position: A bilobed organ lying in the anterior mediastinum, between the sternum and the aorta (S2); more precisely in the superior and retrosternal mediastinum, its two lobes converging at the manubrium, with extensions that can reach the neck toward the thyroid (S3). It develops from the ventral third pharyngeal pouch (S3).
records.structure: The thymus is enclosed in a capsule whose trabeculae divide it into lobules; each lobule has a cortex densely packed with thymocytes and a less densely populated medulla (S2). The release carries the organ and its two lobes only — no lobule, cortex or medulla concept exists (probe-verified).
records.function: A primary lymphoid organ: the thymus is where T cells (thymocytes) mature, as bone marrow is where B cells mature (S2).
records.age_changes: Thymic involution begins after puberty: thymic tissue is lost at roughly 3% per year until about age 35–45, then at roughly 1% per year (S2).

records.name: Lymphatic drainage pathway
verify: no BP3D 4.0 concept exists for this structure (probe-verified over all six release tables by tools/lymph_map.py); the record is sourced text only and links no geometry — this holds for every station of the pathway: no capillary, vessel, trunk or duct of the lymphatic system exists in the release, and the thoracic duct's absence was already probe-verified by Milestone 5 against the same tables
ta_name: not asserted — no TA2 term list was consulted in this session
records.note: The pathway is the system the dataset does not carry: it exists here as sourced clinical text only, in the order the consulted source gives.
sequence: lymphatic capillaries — blind-ended terminal lymphatics in the tissues, where lymph forms
lymphatic vessels — valved collecting vessels, bead-like where their valves constrict them; lymph passes through lymph nodes along the way
lymphatic trunks — the great collecting trunks of the body regions
collecting ducts — the right lymphatic duct and the thoracic duct
the subclavian vein at the junction of the jugular and subclavian veins, where lymph re-enters the blood
records.function: About 20 litres of plasma are filtered out of the blood each day; about 17 litres are reabsorbed and the remaining roughly 3 litres become lymph, which this pathway returns to the venous blood (S2). The system has no central pump: lymph is moved by skeletal muscle action and breathing, and one-way valves prevent backflow (S2). Superficial lymphatics follow the veins and deep lymphatics follow the arteries (S2).
records.ducts_and_territories: The right lymphatic duct drains the right side of the head, the right thorax and the right upper limb into the right subclavian vein. The thoracic duct drains everything else into the left subclavian vein; it begins just beneath the diaphragm in the cisterna chyli, which receives the right and left lumbar trunks and the intestinal trunk (S2). In the small intestine, specialised lymphatics — the lacteals — carry the milky fat-laden lymph called chyle (S2).

records.name: Lymph nodes and lymphoid tissue
verify: no BP3D 4.0 concept exists for this structure (probe-verified over all six release tables by tools/lymph_map.py); the record is sourced text only and links no geometry — no lymph node, tonsil or MALT concept of any kind exists in the release
ta_name: not asserted — no TA2 term list was consulted in this session
records.note: The filtering tissue of the system, carried as sourced text; the geometry layer has none of it.
records.nodes: The body carries roughly 500–600 lymph nodes — small, bean-shaped organs that act as filters of the lymph, clustered near the groin, the armpits, the neck, the chest and the abdomen (S2). Within a node, lymph enters by afferent vessels, passes through the subcapsular sinus, the cortex — which holds follicles with germinal centres — and the medulla with its cords and sinuses, and leaves by efferent vessels (S2).
records.tonsils: The tonsils are lymphoid nodules arranged along the inner surface of the pharynx: the pharyngeal tonsil at the roof of the posterior wall of the superior nasopharynx — called the adenoid when swollen — and the palatine tonsils on either side; they carry an incomplete capsule and tonsillar crypts (S2).
records.malt: Beyond the nodes, lymphoid follicles aggregate under mucous membranes as mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue (MALT) across the gastrointestinal tract, breast, lungs and eyes (S2). In the small intestine these aggregates are Peyer's patches, whose M (microfold) cells sample the gut lumen; the appendix also carries MALT, and bronchus-associated lymphoid tissue (BALT) sits along the bifurcations of the bronchi (S2). The appendix itself is the digestive module's record (Milestone 11); no MALT structure has a concept in the release.
